primitives: finite group element on each oriented edge, inverse on the reversed edge

assumptions.text: the set function is of second order (additive in pairs of walks)
assumptions.note: for one weight function applied to all walks order one cannot depend on gains; returning walks admit a first-order class-function weight without interference (Lemma 3.1, revised; Directors A, B, G); higher even orders exist; edition Z4: if events are sets of histories, a rule adding over end vertices a function of the modulus of the summed gains is consistent only for the square on the signed line and only for the second power on a norm-preserving gain digraph with merging walks (G10-01-03, G10-01-04), and the first-order weighting of returning walks is excluded (G10-01-02); with trivial gains the count is consistent; edition Z7: the carrier must have merging walks; on the countable binary tree every rule of the form is the count (Director G); edition Z8: which objects are records (end vertex only, or end vertex and gain) is part of this assumption and changes the classification (G10 Corollary 5.7); edition Z9: within pair rules consistency excludes the characters in which -1 acts trivially and leaves the others; faithfulness of the character is not obtained (G10 Theorem 5.8)

assumptions.text: pairs of walks with different end vertices do not contribute
one rule, depending on the two gains only, for all graphs and vertices

assumptions.note: argued from closure under composition by Dowker and Wilkes (2022)

assumptions.text: the group and the irreducible representation
assumptions.note: real, complex and quaternionic types all occur; edition Z6: consistency on histories does not select the character (G10-01-09)

assumptions.text: walk length as the only ordering parameter; common step count in products
events are sets of histories (cylinder sets of unending walks); the rule is a sum over end vertices of a function of the modulus of the summed gains
assumptions.note: added in edition Z4 as the assumptions under which GH1-A1 is derived (paper G10)

derived.text: additive invariant functions: constant weight on open walks, class function of the gain on closed walks
invariant pair rules are class functions of the pair holonomy; strongly positive iff non-negative combination of irreducible characters
I_2 = 2 Re D, I_r = 0 for r >= 3
Hilbert space and transition probability; density under a growth condition (criterion: G8-01-10)
product of gain graphs gives the tensor product at each walk length
recorded walks give the counting measure
independence of the faithful character iff n in {1,2,3,4,6}
identity-indicator measure = coincidence count on the derived covering graph = dimension-weighted mean of the irreducible measures
growth condition holds iff the closed walks of even length realize every group element; the limit space follows the group they realize
an additive invariant rule consistent under continuation is a multiple of the count
signed line: consistent modulus rule is the square
norm-preserving digraph with merging walks: the only consistent power is the second
every finite connected signed carrier that is norm-preserving of degree two: consistent modulus rule is the square
gains in the q-th roots of unity: consistent modulus rules are the combinations of the squared moduli in the conjugate characters; unique exactly for q = 2, 4, 6
positivity: non-negative weights; multiplicativity on products: one conjugate character
signed lift: with the gain recorded the record-sum rule is unique for every order, the mean over the characters in which -1 acts as -1
pair rules with a kernel: consistent exactly when the kernel changes sign under -1; mixtures of the characters in which -1 acts as -1
degree two: consistent kernels change sign under the element of the block relation; G10-01-12 restated for any finite abelian group and any degree

absent: relation between the measures at successive lengths (Directors A, B)
continuous group acting on the limit space
operational meaning of the transition probability
